text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The listed Rolimpex SA food processor and trader will cover more than 12 million zlotys in liabilities of the Ketrzyn-based sugar mill and take over the plant, Rolimpex said.
- Holland's KNB PT paper concern will double its cardboard production in Poland in three years time through facility development and acquisition of new plants, the company's regional director said.
- An average Pole annually drinks 80 litres of tea, which makes Poland Europe's fourth biggest tea market after Great Britain, Turkey and Russia, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's largest insurance firm, Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpeiczen (PZU), firm will publish its mandatory car insurance rates for 1997 in mid-December. The company has already said rates would rise.

- A November new share issue by the Polish-Canadian bank Pol-Can Bank and a capital injection by Germany's Berliner Bank, making it a 10-percent owner, will raise Pol-Can Bank's own capital to 23.6 million zlotys, management said.
NOWA EUROPA

- Almost 32 percent of Polish firms expect their sales to improve in the fourth quarter of 1996, 54.8 say they will remain the same and 8.8 percent expect a decline, a report by the Warsaw School of Economics Economic Development Institute said.
- Seven Polish companies will exhibit electronic, construction and mechanical engineering products at the Paris-based MIDEST 96 international fair starting today.
- The PZL-Warszawa Okecie aircraft maker will deliver Wilga, Koliber, and Orlik planes to buyers in Equador, Panama and Mexico, PZL president Ryszard Leja said.
- The Szczecin shipyard will deliver a 13,700 dead weight tonnage (DWT) container ship to a Cypriot shipowner.
The ship may carry up to 1055 containers.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Lublin-based Daewoo plant will soon start production of 4WD Honker land rover cars, the company said.
- Poland's sugar mills processed around 11.3 million tonnes of sugar beet this year, giving the country over 1.4 million tonnes of sugar by the end of November.
This year's output is expected to reach a record level of 2.2 million tonnes, PAP news agency said.
- Less than 33,000 new flats were offered to buyers this year by the end of September, which showed an 18 percent decline compared with the same period last year, Poland's planning ministry said.
- The Bialystok-based Cezar offset printing plant has received an International Standards Organisation(ISO)-9001 quality certificate for high management and product standards.
- In the years 1991-1995 there were more than one million real estate transactions, 600,000 of which were carried out by individuals, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The Suwalki Special Economic Zone (SSZ) in northeastern Poland officially began last week.
The first 12 investors have recieved licenses to operate in the zone.
ZYCIE
- The financial standing of the average Polish family has improved, with 54 percent of Poles saying they belong to a medium income group, a survey by the CBOS polling institute said.
